title: He was chosen… but still got cut.
paragraphs: He was chosen… but still got cut.
Let that sit.

God called him.
Anointed him.
Used him.
And still—he fell.
I’m talking about King Saul.

He wasn’t random.
He was selected by God Himself (see 1 Samuel 10).

Power.
Position.
Presence.
But something shifted.
He started obeying… halfway.

In 1 Samuel 15, God gave a clear command.
No confusion. No gray area.
Saul partially obeyed.

He kept what looked “good.”
Spared what felt “reasonable.”
And then he said the most dangerous words in spiritual life:
“I did obey the Lord…”
But heaven disagreed.
Here’s the line that should shake us:
“Obedience is better than sacrifice.” (1 Samuel 15:22)

Not performance.
Not ministry.
Not results.
Obedience.

Saul was still called…
but he became disqualified from what God intended for him.

Not because God failed—
but because Saul refused to fully surrender.
But here’s what we miss…
Disqualification is not just about big, public sins.
It’s the slow drift.

Half-truths.
Delayed obedience.
Private compromises nobody claps for.
And that’s where grace walks in.
Because the story doesn’t end with Saul.
It points to a better King.

Jesus Christ—
the One who obeyed fully, even to death (Philippians 2:8).

Where Saul failed, Jesus stood firm.
Where we compromise, Jesus remained pure.

And through Him—
we’re not just warned…
We’re redeemed.
So can you be called and still be disqualified?
Yes.
But you don’t have to stay there.

Because in Christ, failure isn’t final—
repentance rewrites the story.

Come back to full surrender.
Not partial. Not delayed.
Whole.
